summary: The v38 RNG mismatch comes from two skipped calls in apply.c:use_whip, not from a missing fire_damage implementation. When a wielded bullwhip is flicked at an adjacent LAVAWALL, or while the hero stands in lava and flicks without a horizontal direction, C discards fire_damage’s boolean but keeps its object effects and random draw. JavaScript recorded note_unported at both call sites. The existing js/trap_water_damage.js implementation supplies the missing rn2(20) draw at segment 0 step 47; wiring both calls completes the whole source function.

source.branch: wielded bullwhip; after direction handling and proficiency setup, either target tile is LAVAWALL with dz==0, or dz>=0 with no horizontal direction and the hero tile is lava. Both branches splash, invoke fire_damage, discard its boolean, and return ECMD_TIME.
callers: apply.c:4266 doapply BULLWHIP case calls use_whip; js/apply.js:4889 forwards the bullwhip through doapply.
dothrow.c:517 dofire calls use_whip when the wielded bullwhip is the automatic fire action; js/dothrow.js:1986 forwards it through dofire.
dependencies: trap.c:4455-4542 fire_damage is already implemented by js/trap_water_damage.js:355; use its side effects and RNG while discarding the return value at both C call sites.
kick_steed is implemented in js/steed.js. The other calls in use_whip remain explicit gaps: weapon.c:possibly_unwield and trap.c:instapetrify are not changed by this task.

evidence: Queue SHA-256 b9c11158f727865211bf58b47b122f03200c3410c8d91a66b9edc9f6f158442a identifies v38-levitating-whip-over-lava with remainingScreens 0, 48 recorded steps, 48/48 screens and cursors, and 3089/3097 RNG calls. Its saved first mismatch is segment 0 step 47, key ".": C rn2(20)=2 from fire_damage(trap.c:4507), while JS next calls rn2(5)=2.

Read nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:2954-3271 and confirmed the adjacent LAVAWALL branch calls fire_damage(uwep,FALSE,rx,ry), and the standing-lava branch calls fire_damage(uwep,FALSE,u.ux,u.uy); both results are explicitly discarded before returning ECMD_TIME.

js/apply.js:823 and :836 previously called note_unported("trap.c fire_damage"). js/trap_water_damage.js:355 implements the C trap.c:fire_damage body and consumes rn2(20) for ordinary objects after catch_lit.

Production callers are apply.c:4266 doapply and dothrow.c:517 dofire, wired by js/apply.js:4889 and js/dothrow.js:1986. The existing source test file exercises both command dispatches; new assertions pin the two C/JS fire_damage call sites.
